summary: Work in flight, with an end — an upload, an import, a scan.

pairs.dont: Use a progress bar for a reading like MOS or disk usage.
pairs.do: Use Meter for a measurement; Progress is for something finishing.
pairs.why: Progress implies a direction and an end. A value that can go back down reads as work being undone.

pairs.dont: Show 0% while waiting for the server to say how much there is.
pairs.do: Pass value={null} until you know, so it announces as indeterminate.
pairs.why: 0% is a claim that nothing has happened yet. Usually something has — you just cannot measure it.

pairs.dont: Animate a bar to 90% and hold it there while you wait.
pairs.do: Show real progress, or an indeterminate bar, or nothing.
pairs.why: A bar that stalls near the end is worse than no bar: it makes a promise about time and then visibly breaks it.

pairs.dont: Show a bare bar with no idea what it is doing.
pairs.do: Name the work, and give a count when you have one.
pairs.why: A percentage answers "how far", never "how long" or "of what". "420 of 1,000 endpoints" answers all three.

pairs.dont: Stack a progress bar per item in a list of fifty.
pairs.do: Show one bar for the batch, and per-item state as text.
pairs.why: Fifty animating bars are a texture, not information, and they cost more to render than the work being measured.
